notes: This contract pins Umbra's bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 timestamped Send Directed Interaction and timestamped Receive Directed Interaction surfaces to the official C++ declarations exported by the Requirements Lab, along with the subscription declarations exercised by its selector regression. The linked Catch2 scenarios cover lower-bound validation, known-target/declaration routing, constrained-recipient queueing before the grant, timestamp/order/retraction callback fields, pending-fanout suppression, a legal Request Retraction callback for an already-delivered nonconstrained directed recipient, default-by-ownership versus universal delivery, declaration changes before a later TSO callback boundary, a queued payload surviving Time Constrained disable/re-enable with one callback before the matching grant, a live queued payload restored across an untimed save/restore boundary and delivered through Flush Queue Request before Request Retraction, target-departure suppression after a lower-timestamped Delete Object Instance removal, and source-mandated delivery through a connection-loss cutoff while the target and recipient selector remain valid. The API surface also links the paired filesystem and HLA_IMMEDIATE failure matrices for the timestamped Send Directed Interaction pre-admission boundary; those cases retain the official five supplied forms, Null/false failure results, exact exception descriptions, and serials zero through three. The DELETE_OBJECTS late-TAR regression additionally retains the target long enough to deliver its cutoff-marked directed callback before grant, then releases the automatic receive-order removal through the next eligible gate; its unsubscribe companion terminally suppresses the callback and releases that removal without pretending a callback was delivered. The direct selector source remains generically mapped (RL-028), the §5.13 continuation candidate used for stale-callback suppression is mis-owned by the Lab (RL-080), the lifecycle relation gap is recorded in RL-134, and the save/restore relation gap is recorded in RL-135. Directed DDM, alternate advance modes, complete save/restore semantics, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
